title: First records with the Ellington orchestra: Jazz Party and a Hodges date
summary: They sort out whether Jazz Party in 1958 was Jones's first Ellington record, and another Hodges-led date.

story.theme_name: Duke Ellington and his orchestra, as others knew them
story.community_name: Duke Ellington: the band, the man, his men

blocks.x: Tell me about "Jazz Party." Was that in the '50s or the '60s? That was what, in the early '60s?
"Jazz Party," the thing with Dizzy and
Yeah. That was the first time you appeared on record with the Duke Ellington Orchestra, right?
I think so. It was in about '58.
Yeah. I thought it was late '50s.
Yeah. Because there was another time I worked for the Ellington Orchestra, but Johnny Hodges was the leader.
When was -- which was that, which album was that?
This was -- let's see, Strayhorn and all the whole band was there. Oh, boy. We did this in Jersey, on Verve with Creed Taylor.
That wasn't, 'Duke's In Bed,' that was done in Chicago, wasn't it?
It was done in New Jersey.
No, but the album that was called, 'Duke's In Bed,' on Verve, I think was recorded in Chicago, so that wouldn't have been the one.
That was the band without Duke, and I think Strays was on piano there.
Yeah. Well, no, I played piano on this one, but the one with, 'Jazz Party,' I -- I just happened to go by the studio. It was at Columbia, in New York, you know?
